---
title: "Reference"
description: "Every option the atelier project type contributes, and the extension keys it reads."
---

This page lists what `project.type: atelier` sets on your behalf and the keys you can set yourself.

## Extension options

These go under `extensions.atelier` in `_quarto.yml`.
Each icon and manifest tag is emitted only when its key is set, while `theme-color` also follows the brand.

| Option             | Description                                                                         |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `site-url`         | Base URL for `<meta property="og:url">`. Anchor it to `website.site-url`.           |
| `icon`             | Path to an SVG icon, emitted as `rel="icon"` with `type="image/svg+xml"`.           |
| `apple-touch-icon` | Path to a 180x180 PNG, emitted as `rel="apple-touch-icon"`.                         |
| `manifest`         | Path to a web app manifest, emitted as `rel="manifest"`.                            |
| `version`          | Text of the version pill, shown next to the title in the navbar or at the top of the sidebar. With no `version`, there is no pill. |
| `mode`             | `documentation` (the default) or `workshop`. Set it once in `_quarto.yml`. A folder `_metadata.yml` or a page front matter can also set it. See [Workshop mode](workshop.qmd). |
| `sidebars`         | The aliases of the `website.sidebar` entries that Atelier reads, such as `- *course`. Each alias must be in the same YAML file as its anchor. |
| `theme-color`      | Browser UI tint (Safari toolbar, Android address bar, installed web app title bar), one colour per scheme, each emitted with a `prefers-color-scheme` media query. Each scheme falls back to `color.background` of the `_brand.yml` for that mode, which is the page background of the matching bundle; set a scheme only to override it. |

: Keys under `extensions.atelier`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[22,78]"}

Paths are relative to the site root.
Quarto's website resource resolver prefixes each page's offset to the project root, so the same value resolves at the root, from a subdirectory such as this page, and from the 404 page.

```yaml
website:
  site-url: &site-url https://example.com/my-project
extensions:
  atelier:
    site-url: *site-url
    icon: assets/icons/icon.svg
    apple-touch-icon: assets/icons/apple-touch-icon.png
    manifest: site.webmanifest
    theme-color:
      light: "#F5F7FA"
      dark: "#0B1220"
```

The anchor is needed because Quarto keeps the `website` block out of the metadata it hands to Lua filters.

## Website defaults

The project type sets these under `website`, and any of them can be overridden in your own `_quarto.yml`.

| Key                                         | Value                                  |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `repo-actions`                              | `[edit, issue]`                        |
| `repo-link-target`, `repo-link-rel`         | `_blank`, `noopener noreferrer`        |
| `open-graph.locale`                         | `en_GB`, matching the format's `lang`  |
| `twitter-card.card-style`                   | `summary_large_image`                  |
| `page-navigation`, `back-to-top-navigation` | `true`                                 |
| `llms-txt`                                  | `true`                                 |
| `search`                                    | Overlay search in the navbar           |
| `navbar`, `page-footer`                     | On, with the footer border on          |

: Keys the project type sets under `website`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[46,54]"}

It also sets `project.output-dir` to `_site`.
It also sets `respect-user-color-scheme: true` at the project level, so that the preview page of an embedded notebook follows the colour scheme of the reader.
As a result, this value applies to every format in the project, not only to `atelier-html`.

Neither bar sets `background` or `foreground`: the chrome palette drives both, and `$atelier-chrome` decides whether it follows the colour scheme or is pinned to `light` or `dark`.

A `website.sidebar` of your own is styled rather than configured: a `style: docked` sidebar is painted from the `--atelier-sidebar-*` tokens, which default to the navbar ones, and a `style: floating` sidebar takes the same tokens as a card with a border and rounded corners.
`website.sidebar` can also be a list of sidebars, each with an `id`.
A page uses the sidebar that lists it, and a workshop sidebar is also named in `extensions.atelier.sidebars`.
This site sets `navbar: false` and gives the docked sidebar the navigation and the search; `--profile navbar` renders the same pages with the navbar instead.

## Layouts and modes

The layout comes from `website.navbar`, and the mode from `extensions.atelier.mode`.
The table in [The workshop chrome](workshop.qmd#the-workshop-chrome) shows what each layout gives each mode.

## Format defaults

The project type sets `format: atelier-html`.
Configure it by that name: declaring `format: html` replaces it rather than configuring it.

| Key                          | Value                                               |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `lang`                       | `en-GB`                                             |
| `date-format`                | `dddd[, the] Do [of] MMMM, YYYY`                    |
| `theme`                      | The chrome palette, `brand`, and the Atelier stylesheet, light and dark |
| `syntax-highlighting`        | `arrow-light` and `arrow-dark`                      |
| `toc`, `toc-depth`           | `true`, `3`                                         |
| `anchor-sections`            | `true`                                              |
| `code-copy`, `code-overflow` | `true`, `wrap`                                      |
| `code-link`                  | `false`                                             |
| `link-external-newwindow`    | `true`                                              |
| `respect-user-color-scheme`  | `true`                                              |
| `canonical-url`              | `true`                                              |
| `grid`                       | 300px sidebar, 1000px body, 300px margin            |

: Keys the project type sets on `atelier-html`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[30,70]"}

It also bundles fourteen scripts into every page, after the body.
They are the current year, the external-link marks, the ordinal dates, the accessibility fixes, the navbar tooltips, the page chrome, the course model, the reading bar, the course, the announcement bar, the table of contents card, the title block, the code blocks, and the listings.
Replacing the format with `html` drops all fourteen, which is what the `id="navbar-tooltips"` check on the [home page](index.qmd) looks for.

Code blocks show on a tinted surface, with a border and an inset.
If you set `code-block-bg: false` under `format.atelier-html`, the tint is not shown and code blocks show as outlines.
A block with a `filename` keeps the surface of its code window.
The border and the inset stay, so the code stays separate from the text around it.
The tint always comes from the brand colours, so a colour value for `code-block-bg` has no effect.
The same is true for `typography.monospace.background-color` and `typography.monospace-block.background-color` in `_brand.yml`, which set `code-block-bg`.
The code surface comes from the brand colours, so the contrast of the syntax highlighting colours on it depends on your brand.

The muted text that Quarto styles on the page, such as the previous and next page links, comes from the page colours and has a contrast of at least 4.5:1 against the page.
To change it, set `$atelier-text-muted` in a project stylesheet under `format.atelier-html.theme`.

## Preset variables

Set these variables under `defaults.bootstrap.defaults` in `_brand.yml`.
[Presets](brand.qmd#presets) describes the three presets.

| Variable                       | Default   | Effect                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------ | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `atelier-preset`               | `default` | The preset: `default`, `quarto`, or `terminal`. Any other value stops the build.            |
| `atelier-terminal-decoration`  | `true`    | The decoration of the `terminal` preset. `false` turns it off. It has no effect on the other presets. |

: Variables that set the preset. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[28,14,58]"}

The variable `atelier-highlighting` is a map of the token colours of each preset and colour scheme.
Do not set it.
The script `scripts/generate-highlighting.py` writes it from the `.theme` files in `_extensions/atelier/highlighting/`.

## Embedded extensions

Atelier contains twelve extensions, so you do not install them yourself.
The `atelier-html` format runs their filters and shortcodes on each HTML page.
The shortcodes work on HTML pages only: on a page in another format, such as Typst, Quarto stops with "Shortcode 'iconify' not found".
Atelier needs Quarto 1.11.9 or later, the first stable 1.11 release.
Older releases remove the `extensions` options of the project from a page that sets `extensions` in its front matter.

| Extension                                                             | What it does                                                                                         | Options under                |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| [iconify](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-iconify)                 | Adds the `{{{< iconify >}}}` shortcode, for icons from the Iconify sets.                             | `extensions.iconify`         |
| [gitlink](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-gitlink)                 | Shows a repository widget in place of a navbar item or sidebar tool with the href `#gitlink-widget`. | `extensions.gitlink`         |
| [code-window](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-code-window)         | Shows a code block that has a `filename` in a window frame with a title bar.                         | `extensions.code-window`     |
| [toc-depth](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-toc-depth)             | Sets the table of contents depth below a heading, with the `toc-depth` attribute.                    | `extensions.toc-depth`       |
| [mobile-toc](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-mobile-toc)           | Shows the table of contents in a bottom sheet on narrow screens, opened from a pill.                 | none                         |
| [collapse-output](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-collapse-output) | Puts cell output in a collapsible block, with the `output-fold` cell option.                         | `extensions.collapse-output` |
| [div-reuse](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-div-reuse)             | Shows the content of one div again in another, with the `reuse` attribute.                          | `extensions.div-reuse`       |
| [highlight-text](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-highlight-text)   | Colours a span of text, with the `fg`, `bg`, and `bc` attributes.                                    | `extensions.highlight-text`  |
| [offset-headings](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-offset-headings) | Moves a heading and the headings below it, with the `offset-headings-by` attribute.                  | `extensions.offset-headings` |
| [preview-colour](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-preview-colour)   | Shows a swatch next to a colour in inline code. The swatch is a button that copies the colour.       | `extensions.preview-colour`  |
| [prism](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-prism)                     | Applies an attribute in one format only, with a format prefix such as `atelier-html:style`.          | `extensions.prism`           |
| [remember](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-remember)               | Offers to return a reader to the place where they stopped, in a banner below the page title.         | `extensions.remember`        |

: Extensions that Atelier contains. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[22,56,22]"}

Each extension keeps its own defaults, and its repository lists its options.
Atelier changes three defaults.
gitlink shows only its widget, and does not change the references in your text.
Code Window shows a window only for a block that has a `filename`, and does not make a label from the language of the other blocks.
remember does not offer to resume on the home page (`index.qmd`) or the 404 page (`404.qmd`).
To turn reference rewriting on, or to give every block a window, set:

```yaml
extensions:
  gitlink:
    enabled: true
  code-window:
    auto-filename: true
```

Quarto adds a `page-exclude` list of your site to the list of Atelier.
You can exclude more pages, but you cannot make remember work on the home page or the 404 page again.
Write each entry as a source file, relative to the project:

```yaml
extensions:
  remember:
    page-exclude:
      - changelog.qmd
      - drafts/*.qmd
```

prism compares its prefix with the name of the output format.
On an Atelier site, that name is `atelier-html`, so write `atelier-html:style`.
The prefix `html:` does not match an Atelier page.

### Upgrade from separate copies

If your project has its own copy of one of these extensions, remove it from `_extensions/` and remove its name from your `filters` list.
Quarto looks up the names in your `filters` list in your own `_extensions/` only, so it then runs your copy and the embedded copy, and your copy's shortcodes replace the embedded ones.
Keep your options under `extensions:`: the embedded copies read them.

## Page keys

| Key                    | Effect                                                                                    |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `description`          | Fills `<meta name="description">` and Quarto's `og:description`.                          |
| `subtitle`             | Used for the description tags when `description` is absent.                               |
| `description-meta`     | Used as written, in preference to both. |
| `extensions.atelier.duration` | The `duration` of a workshop page: `25 min`, `1 h`, `1 h 30 min`, or a number of minutes. See [Modules and durations](workshop.qmd#modules-and-durations). |
| `canonical-url: false` | Drops the canonical link. Set it on a page served from more than one URL, like `404.qmd`. |

: Front matter keys the project type reads. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[24,76]"}

A page with none of the first three gets no description tag at all, so give every page a `description` or a `subtitle`.

`og:url` is emitted for every page except `404.html`, which is served from any URL depth and so claims none of its own.

## Language keys

Atelier writes the text of its chrome from `language` keys.
Atelier ships this text in English and in French, in `_language.yml` and `_language-fr.yml`.
Quarto uses the French file when `lang` starts with `fr`, and the English file for all other languages.

To change a text, set its key under `language` in `_quarto.yml`, in a `_metadata.yml`, or in the front matter of a page.
In the text, `{n}`, `{m}`, `{h}`, `{date}`, `{time}`, and `{site}` are placeholders that Atelier replaces with a value.
Keep each placeholder in your own text.
An empty value removes the text.

```{.yaml filename="_quarto.yml"}
language:
  atelier-next: "Next page"
  atelier-previous: "Previous page"
```

| Key                              | English                              | French                                      |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| `atelier-announcement-info`      | `Info`                               | `Information`                               |
| `atelier-announcement-warning`   | `Warning`                            | `Avertissement`                             |

| `atelier-announcement-success`   | `Success`                            | `Succès`                                    |
| `atelier-announcement-notice`    | `Notice`                             | `Avis`                                      |
| `atelier-announcement-region`    | `Announcement`                       | `Annonce`                                   |
| `atelier-toc-reading-time`       | `{n} min read`                       | `{n} min de lecture`                        |

| `atelier-reading-bar`            | `Reading navigation`                 | `Navigation de lecture`                     |

These Quarto keys also change text in the chrome of Atelier: `toggle-dark-mode`, `toggle-navigation`, `search-label`, `navigation-site-label`, `toc-title-website`, and `announcement-dismiss-label`.
Quarto translates them.
To change one of these texts, set the Quarto key.

### Add a language

1. Copy `_language-fr.yml` from `_extensions/mcanouil/atelier/` to the root of your project, for example as `_language-de.yml`.
2. Translate each value, and keep the placeholders.
3. Set `language: _language-de.yml` in `_quarto.yml`.

The default `date-format` of Atelier has the English words "the" and "of".
For a site in another language, set your own format, for example `date-format: "dddd D MMMM YYYY"`.

Quarto provides the keys of the title block labels.
In workshop mode, the `atelier-workshop-*` keys above replace them, as the [Workshop mode](workshop.qmd#title-block-labels) page shows.

| Key                              | Default                              |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `title-block-author-single`      | `Author`                             |
| `title-block-author-plural`      | `Authors`                            |
| `title-block-published`          | `Published`                          |
| `title-block-modified`           | `Modified`                           |

: The `language` keys of Quarto for the title block labels. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[50,50]"}

## Framed embeds

`.embed-art` frames an embedded document or an image as a tilted card, centred without a wrapper.

```markdown
![](handout.pdf){.embed-art loading="lazy" title="Typst PDF rendered from the demo source"}
```

Pandoc writes an image whose target is not an image as a bare `<embed>` carrying the attributes, so the class applies to `<embed>` and `<img>` alike and every declaration lands on the element itself.
On an `<embed>`, `title` is what gives it an accessible name; `loading="lazy"` is honoured on an `<img>` but has no effect there.

The card takes the shape of what it frames, never wider than the column, with the same padding on all four sides.
An `<img>` is framed at its own dimensions, and an `<embed>` at whatever `width` and `height` you give it:

```markdown
![](handout.pdf){.embed-art width=800 height=600}
```

An `<embed>` is the one case with nothing to follow when you give it no size, because a nested browsing context does not report the dimensions of the document inside it.
These two properties are what it falls back to, and they have no effect on an image or on an `<embed>` with a `width`.

| Property                    | Default | Effect                                        |
| --------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `--atelier-embed-art-width` | `560px` | Width of an `<embed>` with no `width` of its own. |
| `--atelier-embed-art-ratio` | `1.5`   | Shape of that fallback, as width over height. |

: Properties that size an `<embed>` with no width of its own. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[34,12,54]"}

One property applies to every card.

| Property                   | Default    | Effect                                              |
| -------------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `--atelier-embed-art-tilt` | `-1.25deg` | Resting rotation, relaxed toward straight on hover. |

: The property that applies to every card. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[32,14,54]"}

The frame, the offset shadow, and the card background are drawn from the page ink and paper, so they follow the colour scheme.
Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the card holds its resting angle and does not react to hover at all.

## Landing page

Atelier has opt-in classes for a landing page: a hero, feature rows and a card grid.
Write each block as a fenced div, on a page with `page-layout: full` and `title-block-style: none`.
The [Landing page](landing.qmd) guide shows each block and its Markdown, and the [home page](index.qmd) of this site uses them.

```markdown
::: {.atelier-landing}

::: {.atelier-hero .gradient}

::: {.atelier-hero-text}

# Project name

[One sentence that says what the project does.]{.atelier-lead}

:::

:::

:::
```

| Block        | Classes                                                                                                                 | Modifiers                                                |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Container    | `.atelier-landing`                                                                                                      | None.                                                    |
| Hero         | `.atelier-hero`, with the parts `.atelier-hero-text`, `.atelier-hero-figure`, `.atelier-eyebrow`, `.atelier-lead` and `.atelier-actions` | `.split`, `.centred`, `.banner` and `.gradient`           |
| Feature row  | `.atelier-feature`, with the parts `.atelier-feature-text` and `.atelier-feature-figure`                                 | `.reverse`                                               |
| Legend       | `.atelier-legend` around an ordered list, with `.atelier-detail` spans                                                  | None.                                                    |
| Cards        | `.atelier-cards`, which holds `.atelier-card` divs                                                                       | `.compact`                                               |

: Classes and modifiers of the landing page blocks. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[16,56,28]"}

| Modifier    | Effect                                                                                                    |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.split`    | Puts the text part and the figure part side by side. A hero has this layout when it has no other layout modifier. |
| `.centred`  | Centres the text part, in one column. A centred hero has no figure part.                                  |
| `.banner`   | Puts the hero on a tinted surface with a border.                                                          |
| `.gradient` | Fills the hero title (the h1 or the h2) with a gradient that starts at the primary colour.               |
| `.reverse`  | Puts the figure part of a feature row on the left.                                                        |
| `.compact`  | Makes smaller cards, with the icon and the heading on one line.                                           |

: Modifiers of the landing page blocks. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[16,84]"}

The container sets the width of the blocks.
On a page that has the container, Atelier hides the title block, because the hero shows the h1.
The title of the hero is an h1, or an h2 on a page that has its own h1.
Each block stacks into one column below the `md` breakpoint, and a reversed feature row shows its text part first.

Each colour of the gradient has a contrast of 4.5:1 or more against the page, in each colour scheme.
If a colour cannot have this contrast, the hero title uses the primary colour only.
In print and in forced colours mode, the hero title is plain text.
Nothing in the blocks moves, so the reduced motion setting has no effect on them.

A card holds an icon, a heading, one sentence and one link.
The link covers the whole card, and the focus ring of the link goes around the card.
Put only one link in a card, and write link text that says where the link goes.
A compact card has no sentence: put its link in the heading.

These Sass variables set the geometry.
Set them in the `defaults` layer of a project stylesheet.

| Variable                         | Default                    | Effect                                                     |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `$atelier-landing-max-width`     | `1140px`                   | Maximum width of the container.                            |
| `$atelier-landing-gap`           | `3rem`                     | Space between the two parts of a hero or a feature row.    |
| `$atelier-hero-title-size`       | `clamp(2.2rem, 5vw, 3.4rem)` | Font size of the hero title.                             |
| `$atelier-hero-figure-max-width` | `320px`                    | Maximum width of the image in the hero figure.             |
| `$atelier-hero-gradient-shift`   | `40deg`                    | Hue difference between the first and the last gradient colour. |
| `$atelier-card-min-width`        | `13rem`                    | Minimum width of a card column.                            |

: Sass variables of the landing page blocks. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[34,26,40]"}

These Sass variables set the colours.
Atelier calculates each default from the brand for each colour scheme.
The gradient check above also applies to gradient colours that you set.

| Variable                         | Default                                                 | Effect                                 |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `$atelier-landing-accent`        | `$primary`, moved to 4.5:1 against the page             | Eyebrow, legend numbers, card hover.   |
| `$atelier-landing-muted`         | `$text-muted`, moved to 4.5:1 against the page          | Lead and legend detail text.           |
| `$atelier-landing-surface`       | `body-mix(95%)`                                         | Card and banner surface.               |
| `$atelier-landing-border`        | `var(--atelier-border)`                                 | Card, banner and feature row borders.  |
| `$atelier-card-muted`            | `$text-muted`, moved to 4.5:1 against the card surface  | Card text.                             |
| `$atelier-card-link`             | `$link-color`, moved to 4.5:1 against the card surface  | Card link.                             |
| `$atelier-hero-gradient-start`   | `$atelier-landing-accent`                               | First colour of the title gradient.    |
| `$atelier-hero-gradient-middle`  | The mix of the first and last colours, moved to 4.5:1   | Middle colour of the title gradient.   |
| `$atelier-hero-gradient-end`     | `$primary` with the hue shift, moved to 4.5:1           | Last colour of the title gradient.     |
